Q11: How difficult was MATES item 5: Effect size statistic/measure reporting to implement?
Q10:
Provide feedback and suggest rewording of the following item (if necessary):

MATES item 5: Effect size statistic formula reporting

Question
Do the authors report the formula (or reference for formula) for the effect size statistic/measure used (e.g., Zr, Hedge’s g, Cohen’s d, or lnRR) in the manuscript or supplementary material?

Criteria for ‘Yes’
The authors have reported the formula (or reference for formula) for the effect size statistic/measure used in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘No’
The authors have not reported the formula (or reference for formula) for the effect size statistic/measure used in the manuscript or supplementary material.

Criteria for ‘Not Applicable’
There is no ‘Not Applicable’ option for MATES item 5.
Some may use correlations or percentages etc where a formula isn't necessarily required
It was often hard to find this information.
Most information can be obtained in the methodology part. However, sometimes the authors did not provide the formula for the effect size reporting.

Some studies would extract means of a given variable (arm-based meta-analysis), or effect sizes that were already calculated in primary studies. In the former, there is no formula needed and it is not technically an "effect size" sensu stricto; and in the latter, the effect sizes are already available and the formulas are likely in the original studies (and may vary between studies). I think it is relevant to have an "NA" category here for these cases.
Do we systematically need a formula when synthesizing information extracted directly from primary studies (i.e., when the authors have not done any recalculations or other modifications)?
